title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident is an example of deliberate data poisoning aimed at AI retrieval and training pipelines. A fabricated institution was constructed specifically to produce high-volume, citation-formatted content on contested political topics, with the goal of having that content treated as credible source material by AI systems. The mechanism exploited a known vulnerability: AI chatbots and training pipelines often cannot distinguish the institutional legitimacy of a source from its surface formatting.

The failure sits at the data-sourcing stage of AI deployment, before any model inference occurs. Systems that ingest or cite web content have no reliable way to verify that a named institution exists, that its funding is disclosed, or that its output represents genuine research rather than coordinated messaging. Catching this would have required either pre-ingestion audits of source provenance or post-hoc detection of anomalous publication patterns, specifically 124 reports in eight days from a previously unknown organization.

What is not established is whether any major AI system actually incorporated or cited this content, or whether the operation measurably changed AI outputs on the relevant topics. The reporting describes intent and infrastructure, not confirmed effect.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israel established a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy and funded it to produce pro-Israel propaganda aimed at influencing artificial intelligence chatbots. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words, designed to frame Israel's position on topics like Palestinian prisoner torture, war crimes, and Gaza starvation as neutral research. The reports were formatted to resemble academic work with citations, but consistently presented information in ways that undermined criticism of Israel. The operation was part of a broader, multimillion-dollar Israeli government campaign to manipulate AI systems.

The effort involved tens of millions of dollars routed through the European advertising company Havas Media to multiple American contractors, including Clock Tower X run by former Trump strategist Brad Parscale. Researchers found the Hanover Institute site was built using platforms designed to optimize content for AI citation and training data repositories. Israeli officials have privately expressed doubts about whether such campaigns can overcome the underlying political factors affecting American public opinion, with recent polling showing declining American support for Israel, particularly among younger voters and Democrats.
